name: Audre Lorde
summary: Audre Lorde was a self-described Black lesbian feminist socialist whose essays argue that racism, sexism, homophobia and class oppression are interlocked and must be fought together, without erasing differences among those oppressed. She opposed US intervention in Grenada, Central America and support for apartheid, and co-founded Kitchen Table: Women of Color Press. She wrote mostly as a poet and essayist, so many policy questions are not addressed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Condemns cuts to aid for the elderly, dependent children, food stamps and school lunches, and describes welfare mothers living below subsistence.

abortion-legal.rationale: Calls enforced sterilization and unavailable abortions tools of oppression against Black women, i.e. she wants real access to abortion.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Only a passing mention of nuclear poisons in a list of things to examine; no stated position on nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Treats revolution as a continuing process of change rather than a one-time event, and describes Grenada's 1979 revolution's achievements sympathetically; no explicit endorsement of force.

means-match-ends.rationale: "The master's tools will never dismantle the master's house": the oppressor's methods cannot produce genuine change.

production-for-use.rationale: Criticises a society where the good is defined by profit rather than human need as what creates surplus, oppressed groups.

national-self-determination.rationale: On Grenada she says it is Grenadians' country and that outside imposed solutions are arrogant; writes "a nation decides for itself what it needs".

reason-over-faith.rationale: Counters "I think, therefore I am" with "I feel, therefore I can be free", treating feeling as a source of knowledge and action ("Poetry Is Not a Luxury").

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Writes that all women are exposed to patriarchal oppression and defines sexism as the belief in one sex's inherent superiority with a right to dominance.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Insists on relating across differences "as equals" and that freedom cannot belong to one group without the others being free.

defeat-communism.rationale: Argues the supposed threat of socialism is nothing like as destructive as racism, and that Black Americans have bought a government line against it; she calls herself a socialist.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Says the profit economy needs outsiders as surplus people, including women, but also that abolishing capitalism alone would not end sexism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Lists lesbians and gay men as targets of the New Right threatened with imprisonment and death, and campaigns against heterosexism; she opposes criminalisation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Argues in "Age, Race, Class, and Sex" and "The Master's Tools" that racism, sexism, homophobia and classism are inseparable and must be fought together; names herself a Black lesbian feminist socialist.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Argues feminist theory fails without attention to differences of race, class, sexuality and age among women.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Rejects the fashionable separation of the spiritual from the political in "Uses of the Erotic".

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: In 1983-84 essays she describes racism as the pervasive, destructive force in Black Americans' lives (lynchings rising, Black youth unemployment, government racism).

material-over-identity.rationale: Rejects the view that Black women's problems derive only from the capital-labour contradiction; racism and sexism must be fought in their own right.

notes: Full text of Sister Outsider (1984) searched theme by theme. A Burst of Light and The Cancer Journals are borrow-only and could not be downloaded, so her later 1980s statements (apartheid, health politics) are not covered. Not searched further: votes/record (none; she held no office).
